introduction: This spec defines the operational layer for carry-patch workspaces: the integration branch rebuild algorithm, git rerere conflict-resolution replay, upstream merge detection via sync extension, and a status dashboard for monitoring patch stack health. Note: requirements referencing external library APIs (go-git, apikit, GitRunner) are based on PRD descriptions and should be cross-checked against installed library versions before implementation.

glossary.AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC: Workspace variable (boolean string 'true'/'false') controlling whether a rebuild job is automatically enqueued after a successful sync.
glossary.GitRunner: The hub's internal abstraction for executing git CLI commands safely, with protocol allowlists and environment isolation.
glossary.IsAncestor: GitRunner method wrapping 'git merge-base --is-ancestor' to check if one commit is an ancestor of another.
glossary.REBUILD_STRATEGY: Workspace variable controlling how patches are applied during rebuild: 'rebase' (cherry-pick, linear history) or 'merge' (--no-ff, merge commits).
glossary.UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD: Workspace secret holding the password for authenticating against the upstream git remote.
glossary.UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT: Workspace secret holding the personal access token for authenticating against the upstream git remote.
glossary.UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME: Workspace secret holding the username for authenticating against the upstream git remote.
glossary.active: Patch status indicating the patch is in the normal state and should be applied during rebuild.
glossary.autoupdate: The rerere.autoupdate git config option; when true, rerere automatically stages files for which it has a recorded resolution.
glossary.carry_patch: A workspace mode where the hub maintains an integration branch composed of an upstream base plus a stack of carried patch branches.
glossary.carry_patch_workspace: The upstream spec (spec 15) that defines workspace mode, upstream_url, patches table, and resolveUpstreamAuth.
glossary.conflict: Patch status indicating the patch produced an unresolved conflict during the last rebuild attempt.
glossary.conflict_files: List of file paths that had unresolved conflicts when a patch failed during rebuild.
glossary.disabled: Patch status indicating the patch is excluded from rebuild.
glossary.durable_job_queue: The SQLite-backed background job queue (spec 10) used to execute rebuild jobs reliably.
glossary.group_key: The job queue field that serializes jobs targeting the same resource; for rebuilds, set to '<workspace_slug>:<integration_branch>'.
glossary.integration_branch: The git branch that combines the upstream base with all carried patches; always rebuilt from scratch, never edited directly.
glossary.integration_head_sha: The 40-character hex SHA of the HEAD commit on the integration branch after a successful rebuild.
glossary.last_rebuild_result: The outcome of the most recent rebuild job for a given patch: 'success', 'conflict', 'skipped', or null.
glossary.merged_upstream: Patch status indicating the patch branch has been detected as an ancestor of the upstream HEAD, meaning it was merged upstream.
glossary.patch_list: The ordered list of carry patches associated with a workspace, stored in the patches table.
glossary.patch_results: Per-patch outcome array in the rebuild job result, containing status, patch_id, branch_name, position, new_head_sha, and conflict_files for each patch processed.
glossary.patches_merged: Sync response field listing branch names of patches detected as merged upstream during the sync operation.
glossary.patches_table: The database table storing carry patch records (id, workspace_id, branch_name, position, status, etc.) defined by the carry_patch_workspace spec.
glossary.position: The 1-based integer ordering of a patch within the patch list, determining application order during rebuild.
glossary.postimage: A file in an rr-cache subdirectory containing the resolved file content after rerere records a resolution.
glossary.preimage: A file in an rr-cache subdirectory containing the conflicted file content before resolution.
glossary.rebuild_job: A durable background job of type 'rebuild' that executes the integration branch rebuild algorithm.
glossary.rebuild_triggered: Sync response field indicating whether a new rebuild job was enqueued as a result of the sync.
glossary.rerere: Git's reuse recorded resolution feature; records how conflicts are resolved and replays those resolutions automatically on subsequent conflicts.
glossary.rerere_resolution_count: The count of recorded rerere resolutions relevant to files touched by a given patch, shown in the status dashboard.
glossary.resolveUpstreamAuth: Internal function that resolves upstream git credentials from workspace secrets (UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT, UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME, UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD), falling back to origin credentials.
glossary.rr-cache: The .git/rr-cache/ directory where git rerere stores recorded conflict resolutions.
glossary.submitted_by: The identity of the operator who triggered the rebuild, captured in the job payload.
glossary.upstream_head_sha: The 40-character hex SHA of the HEAD commit on the upstream tracking branch at the time of the last fetch.
glossary.upstream_sync: The upstream spec (spec 13) that defines the base sync handler extended by this spec for carry-patch workspaces.
glossary.upstream_tracking_ref: The local git ref that tracks the upstream remote's branch HEAD.
glossary.workspace_slug: The URL-safe identifier for a workspace, used as the dedup key for rebuild jobs.

user_story.goal: trigger a rebuild of the integration branch from upstream HEAD plus all active patches
user_story.benefit: the integration branch always reflects the current upstream plus all carried patches in a reproducible way

acceptance_criteria.action: validate the workspace is in carry_patch mode and is active with a ready clone, capture the REBUILD_STRATEGY workspace variable at enqueue time, enqueue a rebuild_job with type 'rebuild', key set to workspace_slug, and group_key set to '<workspace_slug>:<integration_branch>', and return the job record
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 202 with JSON body containing the job record with status 'queued'

acceptance_criteria.action: fetch from the upstream remote using resolveUpstreamAuth credentials, resolve the upstream tracking ref HEAD, create a temporary branch at that HEAD, collect all patches with status 'active' or 'conflict' in position order, apply each patch using the strategy captured in the job payload, and on full success force-update the integration_branch ref, update integration_head_sha in the database, delete the temporary branch, delete any patches with status 'merged_upstream', and compact remaining positions
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: job completes with structured patch_results payload containing upstream_head_sha, integration_head_sha, strategy, patches_applied, patches_skipped, patches_removed, and per-patch results

acceptance_criteria.action: for each patch, determine commits unique to the patch branch via 'git log --reverse --format=%H <upstream_head>..<patch_branch>', then cherry-pick each commit onto the temporary branch in order, preserving original patch branch refs
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: each successfully applied patch is recorded in patch_results with status 'success' and new_head_sha set to the resulting commit SHA

acceptance_criteria.action: for each patch, merge the patch branch into the temporary branch with --no-ff, producing a merge commit that delineates the patch boundary
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: each successfully applied patch is recorded in patch_results with status 'success' and new_head_sha set to the merge commit SHA

acceptance_criteria.action: allow git rerere with autoupdate to stage resolved files, then run 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U' to check for remaining unresolved conflicts; if all conflicts resolved by rerere, continue the operation; if unresolved conflicts remain, abort the operation, set the patch status to 'conflict' in the database, record conflict_files, delete the temporary branch, and halt the rebuild (fail-fast)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: job fails with structured error containing conflicting patch_id, branch_name, and conflict_files list; integration_branch is not updated
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a cherry-pick or merge produces a conflict during rebuild

acceptance_criteria.action: skip the patch without halting the rebuild, record it in patch_results with status 'skipped', and continue to the next patch
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: patch_results entry has status 'skipped' and null new_head_sha; rebuild continues
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a patch's branch does not exist in the repository during rebuild

acceptance_criteria.action: report patches with status 'merged_upstream' or 'disabled' as 'skipped' in patch_results without attempting to apply them
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: patch_results entries for skipped patches have status 'skipped' and null new_head_sha

acceptance_criteria.action: be registered as type 'rebuild' in the durable_job_queue, be non-retryable on conflict (permanent error), and be retryable on transient failures such as network errors during fetch or temporary filesystem errors

edge_cases.action: reject the rebuild request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the workspace is in 'standard' mode (not carry_patch)

edge_cases.action: reject the rebuild request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the workspace is not active or the clone is not ready

edge_cases.action: reject the rebuild request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: there are no patches with status 'active' or 'conflict' in the patch_list

edge_cases.action: reject the duplicate submission
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 409 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: a rebuild_job with the same workspace_slug key is already queued or running

edge_cases.action: cancel the fetch operation, delete the temporary branch if created, mark the job as failed with a transient error so it is retried
edge_cases.return_contract: job status transitions to 'failed' with a transient error; integration_branch is not modified
edge_cases.error_condition: the upstream fetch hangs or does not return within a reasonable timeout

edge_cases.action: delete the temporary branch to release partial state, do not update the integration_branch ref or integration_head_sha
edge_cases.return_contract: job status transitions to 'failed'; temporary branch is removed; integration_branch is unchanged
edge_cases.error_condition: the rebuild fails midway (e.g., after creating the temporary branch but before completing all patches)

edge_cases.action: complete the rebuild with zero patches applied, force-update the integration_branch to the upstream HEAD, and report patches_applied as 0
edge_cases.return_contract: job completes successfully with patches_applied=0 and integration_head_sha equal to upstream_head_sha
edge_cases.error_condition: the patch_list is empty after filtering out 'merged_upstream' and 'disabled' patches at execution time

edge_cases.action: reject the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the caller lacks the 'rebuilds:write' permission scope

edge_cases.action: fail the fetch step, mark the job as failed with a transient error
edge_cases.return_contract: job status transitions to 'failed' with error indicating authentication failure; integration_branch is not modified
edge_cases.error_condition: resolveUpstreamAuth returns no credentials and the upstream remote requires authentication

requirements.title: Rebuild Job List and Status Endpoints

user_story.goal: list and inspect rebuild jobs for a workspace
user_story.benefit: I can monitor rebuild progress and diagnose failures

acceptance_criteria.action: return the list of rebuild_job records for the workspace ordered by creation time descending
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON array of job records including id, status, created_at, completed_at, strategy, and error fields

acceptance_criteria.action: return the rebuild_job record for the given id, including the full patch_results payload if the job has completed
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON job record; returns HTTP 404 if the job id does not exist for the workspace

edge_cases.action: reject the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the caller lacks the 'rebuilds:read' permission scope

edge_cases.action: return not found to prevent cross-workspace information leakage
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the rebuild id does not belong to the specified workspace_slug

edge_cases.action: return an empty list
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {"jobs": []}
edge_cases.error_condition: the workspace has no rebuild history

user_story.goal: have previously resolved conflicts replayed automatically during rebuild
user_story.benefit: I do not need to manually resolve the same conflict every time the integration branch is rebuilt

acceptance_criteria.action: invoke git rerere (which is enabled with autoupdate=true in the repo config set at clone time) to check for and apply recorded resolutions; run 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U' to determine if any unresolved conflicts remain; if none remain, stage the resolved files and continue the operation
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: rebuild continues to the next patch; the resolved patch is recorded in patch_results with status 'success'
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a cherry-pick or merge produces a conflict

acceptance_criteria.action: abort the cherry-pick or merge, set the patch status to 'conflict' in the patches_table, record conflict_files, delete the temporary branch, and halt the rebuild
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: job fails with structured error; patch_results entry for the conflicting patch has status 'conflict' and non-empty conflict_files
acceptance_criteria.trigger: rerere cannot resolve all conflicts (unresolved conflict markers remain after rerere runs)

edge_cases.action: proceed with rebuild without rerere replay; conflicts are detected and reported normally via 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U'
edge_cases.return_contract: rebuild behaves as if rerere found no resolutions; conflicts cause fail-fast halt
edge_cases.error_condition: rerere is not enabled in the repository config (e.g., workspace was created before rerere config was applied)

edge_cases.action: treat the operation as still conflicted; abort, record all remaining conflict_files from 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U', and halt
edge_cases.return_contract: job fails; conflict_files contains only the unresolved files
edge_cases.error_condition: rerere partially resolves conflicts (some files resolved, others not)

user_story.goal: inspect and clear recorded rerere resolutions for a workspace
user_story.benefit: I can manage stale or incorrect resolutions that would otherwise be replayed incorrectly

acceptance_criteria.action: read the rr-cache directory in the workspace's .git directory, enumerate subdirectories each representing a recorded resolution, derive the path from the preimage or postimage file, and derive recorded_at from the file modification time
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {"resolutions": [{"path": string, "recorded_at": string|null}]}

acceptance_criteria.action: execute 'git rerere forget <pathspec>' via GitRunner for the workspace repository
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 204 on success; returns HTTP 404 if the pathspec has no recorded resolution in rr-cache

edge_cases.action: return an empty resolutions list
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON body {"resolutions": []}
edge_cases.error_condition: the rr-cache directory does not exist or is empty

edge_cases.action: use the Echo *pathspec wildcard route parameter to capture the full path including slashes without requiring URL encoding
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 204 on success with the full path correctly passed to 'git rerere forget'
edge_cases.error_condition: the pathspec contains slashes (e.g., 'src/config.go') and the Echo wildcard parameter does not capture the full path

edge_cases.action: skip that entry or include it with path set to null; do not crash
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200; malformed entries are omitted from the resolutions array
edge_cases.error_condition: a rr-cache subdirectory exists but contains no preimage or postimage file

edge_cases.action: reject the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the caller lacks the 'workspaces:read' permission scope

user_story.goal: sync a carry-patch workspace against upstream and automatically detect merged patches
user_story.benefit: the patch_list stays accurate without manual inspection after each upstream update

acceptance_criteria.action: resolve upstream credentials via resolveUpstreamAuth, fetch from the 'upstream' remote (not 'origin'), compare the new upstream HEAD against the stored upstream_head_sha, advance the upstream_tracking_ref using the same fast-forward logic as the standard sync handler, then check each active patch for upstream merge using IsAncestor
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: sync response includes patches_merged (list of branch names) and rebuild_triggered (boolean) in addition to standard sync fields
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a sync operation is triggered for a workspace in carry_patch mode

acceptance_criteria.action: transition the patch status to 'merged_upstream' in the patches_table and include the branch name in the patches_merged list in the sync response
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: sync response patches_merged array contains the branch name; patch record in database has status 'merged_upstream'
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a patch branch HEAD is determined to be an ancestor of (or equal to) the new upstream HEAD via IsAncestor

acceptance_criteria.action: enqueue a rebuild_job for the workspace; if a rebuild_job with the same workspace_slug key is already queued or running, silently ignore the duplicate and set rebuild_triggered to false in the response
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: sync response has rebuild_triggered=true if a new job was enqueued, rebuild_triggered=false if a duplicate was detected
acceptance_criteria.trigger: sync completes for a carry_patch workspace
acceptance_criteria.condition: at least one patch was transitioned to 'merged_upstream' OR the upstream_tracking_ref advanced, AND AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is 'true' (or not set)

acceptance_criteria.action: do not enqueue a rebuild_job regardless of whether patches were merged or the upstream ref advanced
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: sync response has rebuild_triggered=false
acceptance_criteria.trigger: sync completes for a carry_patch workspace

edge_cases.action: abort the sync, do not modify the upstream_tracking_ref or any patch statuses
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 502 or appropriate error status with JSON error body; no state is mutated
edge_cases.error_condition: the upstream fetch fails due to a network error or authentication failure

edge_cases.action: skip the ancestry check for that patch, leave its status unchanged, and continue checking remaining patches
edge_cases.return_contract: sync completes; the patch with the missing ref is not included in patches_merged
edge_cases.error_condition: IsAncestor returns an error for a specific patch (e.g., the patch branch ref does not exist locally)

edge_cases.action: complete the sync successfully with no patches_merged and no rebuild triggered (unless AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC logic applies for other reasons)
edge_cases.return_contract: sync response has patches_merged=[] and rebuild_triggered=false
edge_cases.error_condition: the upstream HEAD has not changed since the last sync (upstream_head_sha is unchanged)

edge_cases.action: use the standard sync handler behavior without carry-patch extensions; patches_merged and rebuild_triggered fields are omitted from the response
edge_cases.return_contract: standard sync response without carry-patch fields
edge_cases.error_condition: the sync is triggered on a 'standard' workspace

edge_cases.action: enforce a timeout on the fetch operation; if exceeded, abort the sync and return an error
edge_cases.return_contract: returns an error response; upstream_tracking_ref and patch statuses are not modified
edge_cases.error_condition: the upstream fetch hangs and does not return

user_story.goal: view a comprehensive health summary of the patch stack for a workspace
user_story.benefit: I can quickly assess which patches are clean, conflicting, or already merged without running multiple queries

acceptance_criteria.action: aggregate workspace metadata (upstream_url, upstream_head_sha, integration_branch, integration_head_sha, last_sync_at), the most recent rebuild_job record, all patches from the patches_table with their last_rebuild_result and conflict_files from the most recent rebuild, and rerere_resolution_count per patch, then return the combined response
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with JSON body matching the patch-status schema including workspace_slug, workspace_mode, upstream_url, upstream_head_sha, integration_branch, integration_head_sha, last_sync_at, last_rebuild, patches array, and summary counts

acceptance_criteria.action: compute the summary object with total_patches, active, merged_upstream, conflict, and disabled counts derived from the current patches_table state
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: summary counts are accurate and consistent with the patches array in the same response

acceptance_criteria.action: return last_rebuild as null and each patch's last_rebuild_result as null
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with last_rebuild=null and all patch last_rebuild_result fields null
acceptance_criteria.state: no rebuild has been attempted for the workspace

edge_cases.action: reject the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the workspace is not in carry_patch mode

edge_cases.action: reject the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the caller lacks the 'workspaces:read' permission scope

edge_cases.action: return an empty patches array and summary with all counts at zero
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with patches=[] and summary={total_patches:0, active:0, merged_upstream:0, conflict:0, disabled:0}
edge_cases.error_condition: the patches_table is empty (no patches have been added)

edge_cases.action: set rerere_resolution_count to 0 for all patches rather than failing the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with rerere_resolution_count=0 for all patches
edge_cases.error_condition: the rr-cache directory is inaccessible when computing rerere_resolution_count

user_story.goal: submit, list, and inspect rebuild jobs from the command line
user_story.benefit: I can manage rebuild operations without using the REST API directly

acceptance_criteria.action: send POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuild and print the returned job record
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: prints job id and status 'queued' to stdout; exits with code 0 on success, non-zero on error

acceptance_criteria.action: send GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuilds and print the list of rebuild jobs
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: prints tabular or JSON list of rebuild jobs to stdout; exits with code 0 on success

acceptance_criteria.action: send GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id and print the job status and patch_results
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: prints job details including status and per-patch results to stdout; exits with code 0 on success, non-zero if job not found

edge_cases.action: print the error message to stderr and exit with a non-zero exit code
edge_cases.return_contract: error message printed to stderr; process exits with non-zero code
edge_cases.error_condition: the API returns an error response for any rebuild CLI command

edge_cases.action: print usage information and exit with a non-zero exit code
edge_cases.return_contract: usage text printed to stderr; process exits with non-zero code
edge_cases.error_condition: the workspace-slug argument is missing from any rebuild CLI command

user_story.goal: list and forget rerere resolutions from the command line
user_story.benefit: I can manage conflict resolution records without using the REST API directly

acceptance_criteria.action: send GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rerere and print the list of recorded resolutions
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: prints list of resolutions with path and recorded_at to stdout; exits with code 0

acceptance_criteria.action: send DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rerere/*pathspec and print confirmation
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: prints confirmation to stdout on success; prints error to stderr and exits non-zero if pathspec not found

edge_cases.action: append the pathspec as a path segment after /rerere/ without additional URL encoding of slashes, relying on the Echo wildcard route to capture the full path
edge_cases.return_contract: DELETE request reaches the server with the full pathspec; returns HTTP 204 on success
edge_cases.error_condition: the pathspec argument contains slashes and the CLI must construct the DELETE URL correctly

user_story.goal: view the patch stack health dashboard from the command line
user_story.benefit: I can quickly assess workspace patch health without opening a browser or crafting API calls

acceptance_criteria.action: send GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patch-status and print the full status dashboard
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: prints workspace metadata, last_rebuild summary, per-patch status table, and summary counts to stdout; exits with code 0 on success, non-zero on error

edge_cases.action: print the error message to stderr and exit with a non-zero exit code
edge_cases.return_contract: error message printed to stderr; process exits with non-zero code
edge_cases.error_condition: the workspace is not in carry_patch mode and the API returns HTTP 400

correctness_properties.title: Integration branch is always rebuilt from scratch
correctness_properties.for_any: carry_patch workspace with any combination of active, conflict, merged_upstream, and disabled patches
correctness_properties.invariant: after a successful rebuild, the integration_branch ref equals the result of applying all active and conflict patches (in position order, using the captured strategy) onto the upstream_head_sha; no prior integration_branch state influences the result

correctness_properties.title: Fail-fast halts on first conflict
correctness_properties.for_any: rebuild with N patches where patch K (1 <= K <= N) produces an unresolvable conflict
correctness_properties.invariant: the rebuild halts after patch K; patches K+1 through N are not attempted; the integration_branch ref is not updated; the temporary branch is deleted

correctness_properties.title: Rebuild strategy is captured at enqueue time
correctness_properties.for_any: rebuild job enqueued with REBUILD_STRATEGY value S
correctness_properties.invariant: the job executes with strategy S regardless of any subsequent changes to the REBUILD_STRATEGY workspace variable before the job runs

correctness_properties.title: Merged patches are cleaned up after successful rebuild
correctness_properties.for_any: workspace with one or more patches in merged_upstream status at the start of a rebuild
correctness_properties.invariant: after a successful rebuild, all patches that had merged_upstream status are deleted from the patches_table and remaining positions are compacted to be contiguous

correctness_properties.title: Rerere replay is idempotent
correctness_properties.for_any: any number of rebuilds that encounter the same conflict in the same patch
correctness_properties.invariant: if rerere has a recorded resolution for the conflict, each rebuild attempt that encounters that conflict will have it resolved automatically; the rebuild result is the same as if the conflict never occurred

correctness_properties.title: Ancestry-based merge detection is monotonic
correctness_properties.for_any: any patch P and any two consecutive upstream fetches where the upstream HEAD advances from SHA1 to SHA2
correctness_properties.invariant: if P was detected as merged_upstream at SHA1, it remains merged_upstream at SHA2; the merged_upstream status is never reverted by a subsequent sync

correctness_properties.title: Duplicate rebuild enqueue is idempotent
correctness_properties.for_any: any number of concurrent or sequential rebuild submission attempts for the same workspace_slug while a rebuild_job is already queued or running
correctness_properties.invariant: exactly one rebuild_job is active at a time for a given workspace_slug; duplicate submissions are rejected with HTTP 409 or silently ignored (auto-rebuild path) without creating additional jobs

correctness_properties.title: Status dashboard counts are consistent with patch array
correctness_properties.invariant: summary.total_patches equals the length of the patches array; summary.active + summary.merged_upstream + summary.conflict + summary.disabled equals summary.total_patches

correctness_properties.title: Temporary branch is always cleaned up
correctness_properties.for_any: any rebuild execution that creates a temporary branch, regardless of outcome (success, conflict, or unexpected error)
correctness_properties.invariant: the temporary branch does not exist in the repository after the rebuild job terminates

execution_paths.title: Full carry-patch end-to-end: sync, rebuild, status check

steps.action: runs 'afc workspace patch-status <slug>' to confirm patch stack state before sync
sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patch-status to the hub
reads workspace metadata, patches_table, and last rebuild result from the database and returns the aggregated status response
triggers sync by sending POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sync

steps.actor: carry-patch sync handler (this spec, extending upstream_sync spec 13)
steps.action: calls resolveUpstreamAuth (carry_patch_workspace spec 15) to get upstream credentials, fetches from the 'upstream' remote via go-git, advances the upstream_tracking_ref
calls GitRunner.IsAncestor (git_runner_extensions spec 14) for each active patch to detect merged patches; transitions detected patches to 'merged_upstream' in the patches_table

checks AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC workspace variable; enqueues a rebuild_job in the durable_job_queue (spec 10) with key=workspace_slug and group_key='<slug>:<integration_branch>'; returns sync response with patches_merged and rebuild_triggered=true
dispatches the rebuild_job to the rebuild job executor
calls resolveUpstreamAuth, fetches from upstream remote, resolves upstream_tracking_ref HEAD, creates a temporary branch at that HEAD
collects patches with status 'active' or 'conflict' in position order from the patches_table; skips 'merged_upstream' and 'disabled' patches

for each active patch (rebase strategy): calls GitRunner log to find unique commits, then calls GitRunner CherryPick (git_runner_extensions spec 14) for each commit onto the temporary branch; on conflict, invokes rerere and checks 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U'

on full success: force-updates the integration_branch ref to the temporary branch HEAD, updates integration_head_sha in the database, deletes the temporary branch, deletes merged_upstream patches from the patches_table, and compacts positions
runs 'afc workspace patch-status <slug>' to verify the updated integration_head_sha and clean patch stack
returns updated status with last_rebuild showing 'completed', patches_applied count, and all patches showing last_rebuild_result='success'

execution_paths.title: Rebuild conflict: detection, rerere replay, and manual re-trigger

steps.action: sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuild to trigger a rebuild
validates workspace is carry_patch mode, active, and has active patches; enqueues rebuild_job; returns HTTP 202 with job record
dispatches the rebuild_job
applies patches in order; a cherry-pick produces a conflict; rerere (autoupdate=true) stages resolved files; 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U' returns non-empty list
aborts the cherry-pick, sets patch status to 'conflict' in patches_table, records conflict_files, deletes the temporary branch, marks job as failed (permanent error)
sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id to inspect the failure
returns job record with status 'failed' and patch_results showing the conflicting patch with conflict_files
manually resolves the conflict in the patch branch and runs 'git rerere' to record the resolution in rr-cache
sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuild to re-trigger the rebuild

re-applies patches; the previously conflicting cherry-pick now triggers rerere which replays the recorded resolution; 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U' returns empty; rebuild continues and succeeds
force-updates integration_branch, updates integration_head_sha, deletes temporary branch; job completes successfully

execution_paths.title: Rerere resolution management: list and forget

steps.action: sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rerere to list recorded resolutions
reads the rr-cache directory, enumerates subdirectories, reads preimage/postimage files to derive paths and recorded_at timestamps, returns the resolutions list
identifies a stale resolution and sends DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rerere/src/config.go
executes 'git rerere forget src/config.go' via GitRunner in the workspace repository; returns HTTP 204
sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rerere to confirm the resolution was removed
returns updated resolutions list without the forgotten path

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuild called on a workspace not in carry_patch mode
error_handling.behavior: returns HTTP 400 with JSON error body; no job is enqueued

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuild called when workspace is not active or clone is not ready
error_handling.behavior: returns HTTP 400 with JSON error body; no job is enqueued

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuild called when no patches have status 'active' or 'conflict'
error_handling.behavior: returns HTTP 400 with JSON error body; no job is enqueued

error_handling.condition: POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rebuild called when a rebuild_job with the same workspace_slug key is already queued or running
error_handling.behavior: returns HTTP 409 with JSON error body; no additional job is enqueued

error_handling.condition: rebuild job executor encounters an unresolvable conflict during cherry-pick or merge
error_handling.behavior: aborts the operation, sets patch status to 'conflict' in patches_table, records conflict_files, deletes the temporary branch, marks job as permanently failed; integration_branch is not updated

error_handling.condition: rebuild job executor encounters a transient error (network failure during fetch, temporary filesystem error)
error_handling.behavior: marks the job as failed with a retryable error; the durable_job_queue will retry the job; temporary branch is cleaned up if created

error_handling.condition: DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/rerere/*pathspec called for a pathspec with no recorded resolution in rr-cache
error_handling.behavior: returns HTTP 404 with JSON error body; no git command is executed

error_handling.condition: carry-patch sync handler fails to fetch from the upstream remote
error_handling.behavior: aborts the sync; upstream_tracking_ref and patch statuses are not modified; returns an error response to the caller

error_handling.condition: GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patch-status called on a workspace not in carry_patch mode
error_handling.behavior: returns HTTP 400 with JSON error body

error_handling.condition: caller lacks required permission scope for any rebuild, rerere, or patch-status endpoint
error_handling.behavior: returns HTTP 403 with JSON error body; no operation is performed

error_handling.condition: rebuild job executor cannot resolve upstream credentials via resolveUpstreamAuth and the upstream remote requires authentication
error_handling.behavior: fails the fetch step, marks the job as failed with a transient error for retry; integration_branch is not modified
